packs.title: Art, Parks and Stories
packs.promise: Explore Raleigh's art, landscapes and history across separate city outings.

q.s: Let one museum artwork prompt an original form.
st: Choose one displayed artwork and credit its maker and title.
Record one shape or color relationship you observe.
Make an original design with a different subject using that relationship.

q.s: Find how a public park changes the view of the city.
st: From an open public path, choose a view that includes a park foreground and city skyline.
Sketch or describe the two layers without photographing other visitors.
Add one original change you would make to the frame and explain its effect.

q.s: Compare plant forms without leaving the path.
st: Choose two visible plants with different leaf shapes.
Draw or describe each outline without collecting a leaf.
Propose one original design that uses the contrast, without claiming a botanical function you cannot verify.

packs.title: Downtown Lines and Layers
packs.promise: Read downtown Raleigh through public art, squares, museums and historic streets.

q.s: Turn a canopy structure into a small design study.
st: Read the city's credit for Thomas Sayre and the canopy.
From the open plaza, notice one relationship between the steel supports and filtered shade.
Sketch an original shelter pattern that changes that relationship.

q.s: See how paths organize a small public park.
st: Enter by a permitted path and locate the central memorial from a respectful distance.
Identify two path approaches and the edges they connect.
Make a tiny plan showing how the paths frame the central space.

q.s: Use a city artifact to connect past and present.
st: Choose an object in an open gallery and record its exhibit credit or label.
Note what the label establishes about its earlier use.
Name one present-day question the object raises, keeping your inference separate from the label.
